claims.text: A uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates along lamellar phase boundaries will simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The baseline eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The baseline material contains no intentionally introduced nanoscale precipitates.
A tailored single-step thermomechanical treatment can promote in-situ formation of nanoscale coherent precipitates specifically at lamellar interfaces.
The thermomechanical treatment can form the precipitates without changing the overall alloy composition.
The thermomechanical treatment can preserve the alloy's dual-phase lamellar structure.
The engineered structural mediator is a uniform distribution of nanoscale coherent precipitates along lamellar interfaces.
The coherent precipitates hinder dislocation motion through Orowan looping.
Hindering dislocation motion increases yield strength.
The precipitates provide additional dislocation-storage sites.
Additional dislocation storage delays strain localization and thereby enhances ductility.
At room temperature, the treated alloy will have greater yield strength than conventionally processed material.
At room temperature, the treated alloy will sustain more plastic deformation before failure than conventionally processed material.
The simultaneous benefit requires a high-density, coherent, and uniformly distributed precipitate network that does not compromise the lamellar structure.
Nonoptimal precipitate volume fraction or loss of coherence may negate the intended strength and ductility benefits.
The magnitude of the improvements may depend on precipitate-formation kinetics, interfacial stability, precipitate volume fraction, and precipitate size distribution.
